title: cleanGrid
body:
## cleanGrid

Converts any dataset into an unstructured grid and merges coincident points (exactly coincident at the Schemaxis default tolerance 0), optionally removing points used by no cell (Schemaxis default true). Use it to obtain an unstructured grid for operations that need one, or to stitch appended parts. Use clean when the input is polydata and polydata output is wanted.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Structured inputs lose their implicit structure and grow in memory once converted.

Native constructor: `CleantoGrid`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tolerance` | When merging nearby points and not using absolute tolerance (see ToleranceIsAbsolute property), this property specifies the tolerance for performing merging as a fraction of the length of the diagonal of the bounding box of the input data set. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0}` | `0` | `0` |
| `removeUnusedPoints` | Drop points that no cell references, such as orphan nodes left by extraction. Disable it when isolated points carry meaning: a point cloud without vertex cells would otherwise lose every point. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "cleanGrid",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  }
}
```
